scope.excluded_work: all catalog problems and research tracks other than #021/B7, #022/B2, and #023

question: When may a short surface-code memory result count as scalable logical memory, and when may that evidence enter the B7 fault-tolerance resource ledger?

required_fragments: total number of physical qubits required for this encoding is 288

horizon_contract.confidence_method: two-sided Wilson 95 percent upper bound with z=1.959963984540054
horizon_contract.direct_evidence_rule: source experiment rounds must be at least the claimed memory horizon; shorter experiments never become direct horizon evidence by extrapolation
horizon_contract.basis_rule: both X and Z memory must independently pass at the same distance, physical-error setting, horizon, and target
horizon_contract.projection_model: stationary independent logical flips using p_H=(1-(1-2*epsilon)^H)/2; projection is diagnostic only
horizon_contract.statistical_resolution: report the minimum zero-failure direct-horizon shots and qubit-cycle exposure required for the Wilson upper bound alone to clear each target

acceptance_gate.p023_scalable_memory_ready: at least one distance and physical-error pair passes both bases by direct experiments at 1,000 and 1,000,000 rounds with total failure <= 0.01, reports decoder throughput and latency, and survives a declared drift/correlation stress
acceptance_gate.b2_low_overhead_credit_ready: P023 direct-horizon gate passes and a same-condition surface-code versus candidate-code comparison improves physical-qubit-cycle volume by at least 25 percent without weakening failure target, decoder, connectivity, or noise assumptions
acceptance_gate.b7_memory_credit_ready: P023 and B2 gates pass and the existing B7 calibrated dependency-credit gate permits credit
acceptance_gate.failure_action: retain short-memory rows as simulator calibration only; assign zero scalable-memory and B7 resource credit
